findings.title: PR description omits the metrics changes (new decrement + tests)
findings.claim: The PR adds decrement_total_connections and three metrics regression tests, but the description and title only mention the keyspace-setup fix, and validation only runs keyspace_setup_failure tests, never the metrics tests.

findings.title: Repeated log/decrement/clear sequence duplicated at three call sites
findings.claim: The same log, then decrement, then excess_connections.clear() sequence is repeated at connection_pool.rs:674, :1031, :1115; a small clear_excess_connections() helper would prevent the metric and the vec from drifting apart.

findings.title: ConnectionSetupError name easily confused with ConnectionError
findings.claim: ConnectionSetupError is easy to confuse with ConnectionError, and errors.rs already has ConnectionSetupRequestError; since it's a private two-variant enum, a name like OpenedConnectionFailure would be clearer.

findings.title: keyspace_setup_failure_preserves_pool_state builds proxy rules inline instead of reusing…
findings.claim: keyspace_setup_failure_preserves_pool_state builds its proxy rules inline while other tests use start_simulated_node or mock_pool_refiller; the test is about 150 lines and the metrics tests could share more setup.

findings.title: Keyspace-failure path drops the shard-aware fallback that connection errors get
findings.claim: A failed USE on a connection opened with requested_shard: Some(..) doesn't recover the way a shard-aware connect failure does: the Connection error path immediately calls start_opening_connection(None), while the keyspace path only waits for the next scheduled refill with backoff, and the code doesn't indicate this is deliberate.

findings.title: Keyspace failure marks whole pool Broken without distinguishing transient vs permanent…
findings.claim: update_shared_conns(Some(err.into())) makes the whole pool Broken with UseKeyspaceError when the pool is empty and nothing is filling; a transient failure (timeout, IO error) is reported the same as a permanent one (BadKeyspaceName, nonexistent keyspace), and the pool will keep reconnecting and failing USE indefinitely with growing, unbounded backoff.

findings.title: Keyspace check now runs before resharding, an undocumented behaviour change
findings.claim: Previously a connection was resharded first and then had its keyspace set; now a new connection that would trigger a reshard has USE run first. This appears intended and is what makes the 'preserves current pool' test pass, but the description doesn't call it out as a behaviour change.

findings.title: keyspace_setup_failure_triggers_refill doesn't actually prove a refill is scheduled
findings.claim: The test name says 'triggers refill' but it only asserts the need_filling() predicate; it never runs the run loop, so it doesn't prove a refill is actually scheduled.

findings.title: Test's proxy.finish() accepts DriverDisconnected, hiding real proxy errors
findings.claim: keyspace_setup_failure_preserves_pool_state ends with drop(refiller) after proxy.finish(), and the proxy.finish() match accepts DriverDisconnected, which hides real proxy errors.

findings.title: Test combines failure and success USE checks in one test, hiding failures in the second…
findings.claim: The failure and success USE checks share one test, so a failure in the first half hides the second.

findings.title: New public ConnectionError::UseKeyspaceError variant lacks changelog/docs entry
findings.claim: ConnectionError::UseKeyspaceError is a new variant on a #[non_exhaustive] public enum (not a breaking change) but is user-visible through Broken(..), and the PR has no changelog or docs entry despite the description stating documentation changes are not needed.
